title: Porto-systemic encephalopathy types, neurotoxins and astrocyte swelling
guide: Porto-systemic encephalopathy terminology, Types A, B, and C (Type A cerebral edema m/c cause of death, Type C cirrhosis m/c), neurotoxins (ammonia, mercaptans, manganese, GABA, octopamine), colonic glutaminase, non-ionic NH3 diffusion, Alzheimer type-2 astrocytes, glutamine synthetase swelling, and distinction from PMLE type-1 cells.

title: Precipitating triggers, West Haven criteria and diagnostic bedside signs
guide: NH3-increasing triggers (protein, constipation, bleeding, sepsis), alkalosis shifting NH4+ to NH3, diuretic hypokalemia and RAAS activation, sedatives increasing GABA, West Haven covert (minimal positive number connection test, Grade-I sleep reversal) versus overt (Grade-II asterixis, Grade-III clonus/rigidity, Grade-IV decorticate triphasic EEG), and constructional apraxia.

title: Medical management ladder, lactulose MOA and liver transplantation
guide: Lactulose bowel wash 4 times daily (most important), rifaximin 400 mg TDS / 550 mg BD, acarbose, LOLA / branched-chain AA, sodium benzoate NH3 trapping, lactulose three-fold MOA (luminal acidification trapping NH4+, VFA bacterial substrate shift, osmotic laxation), and liver transplantation as final option.
